learningObjectives.title: The motor effect and electromagnetic induction

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.explain: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C).

questions.q: Which equation correctly links potential difference (V), current (I) and resistance (R)?
questions.explain: Potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance (V = IR).

questions.q: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms, symbol Ω.

questions.q: Which of these is a magnetic material?
questions.explain: Iron, cobalt, nickel and steel are the common magnetic materials.

questions.q: Which rule is used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
questions.explain: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the motor-effect force.

questions.q: What happens when two objects carrying the same type of charge are brought close together?
questions.explain: Like charges repel, while unlike charges attract.

questions.q: How should an ammeter be connected to measure the current through a component?
questions.explain: An ammeter is connected in series so the same current flows through it and the component.

questions.q: In which direction do magnetic field lines point outside a bar magnet?
options: From the north pole to the south pole
From the south pole to the north pole
questions.explain: By convention, field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.

questions.q: When a polythene rod is rubbed with a cloth and becomes negatively charged, what has happened?
options: Electrons have moved onto the rod
Protons have moved onto the rod
Neutrons have moved onto the rod
questions.explain: Charging by friction transfers electrons; gaining electrons makes an object negative.

questions.q: How does the current behave in a series circuit?
options: It is the same at every point
It is largest near the battery
questions.explain: In a series circuit the current is identical everywhere as there is only one path.

questions.q: For two components connected in parallel, how does the potential difference across them compare?
options: It is the same across each component
It is shared equally by adding to the supply
It is larger across the smaller resistor
It is zero across each component
questions.explain: Components in parallel share the same potential difference.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a filament lamp as the current through it increases?
options: It increases as the filament gets hotter
It decreases as the filament gets hotter
questions.explain: Higher current heats the filament, increasing resistance so the I–V graph curves.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet?
options: An induced magnet loses its magnetism when removed from the field
A permanent magnet loses its magnetism when removed from the field
An induced magnet is always stronger
A permanent magnet only attracts other magnets
questions.explain: Induced magnetism is temporary and disappears once the external field is removed.

questions.q: How can a potential difference be induced in a wire using a magnet?
options: By moving the wire so it cuts through magnetic field lines
By holding the wire still inside a uniform field
By heating the wire in the field
questions.explain: Electromagnetic induction requires relative movement so field lines are cut.

questions.q: What does the region around a charged object where it can affect other charges represent?
questions.explain: A charged object is surrounded by an electric field that exerts forces on other charges.

questions.q: What is the shape of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying solenoid?
options: Similar to the field of a bar magnet
Circular loops only inside the wire
questions.explain: A solenoid produces a strong, uniform field inside and an external field like a bar magnet.

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a 6 Ω resistor. What is the potential difference across it?
questions.explain: Using V = IR gives V = 2 × 6 = 12 V.

questions.q: A component has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
questions.explain: Rearranging V = IR gives R = V ÷ I = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 Ω.

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows for 5 s. How much charge passes a point in the circuit? (Q = I × t)
questions.explain: Charge Q = It = 2 × 5 = 10 C.
